questions.stem: A linear octasaccharide has molar mass 1024 g/mol. Complete hydrolysis yields ribose (150), 2-deoxyribose (134) and glucose (180). The 2-deoxyribose mass is 58.26% of the total monosaccharide mass after hydrolysis. Find the number of ribose units in one octasaccharide molecule.
conditions: A linear octasaccharide has seven glycosidic links and therefore consumes seven H2O on complete hydrolysis.
Molar masses are in g/mol.

reasoning: One mole octasaccharide gains 7×18=126 g of water on hydrolysis, so total monosaccharide mass is 1024+126=1150 g.
2-Deoxyribose mass is 0.5826×1150≈670 g, which is 670/134=5 mol units. Thus the remaining three units are ribose and glucose.
Let r be ribose units and g=3-r glucose units. 150r+180g=1150-670=480; solving gives r=2 and g=1.
